Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators — overall risk: info.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • Based on the reviewed text, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, malicious setup.py/PEP 517 build hooks, or install-time execution.
  • The @codecs.register and @codecs.register_error usage in cssutils/codec.py appears to be normal library behavior for registering a CSS codec, with no link to credential collection, exfiltration, or persistence.
  • The eval(repr(...)) usage in tests appears to validate object repr round-tripping and is not evidence of malicious install-time or import-time execution.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • Credential theft: No evidence of broad discovery of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI tokens, or similar secrets.
  • Exfiltration: urllib.request.urlopen(request) in cssutils/_fetch.py appears related to expected CSS fetching, such as @import handling; there is no evidence of harvested data upload or attacker-controlled C2 exfiltration.
  • Staging: No evidence of tar/zip/gzip/base64 staging or bundling of harvested files.
  • Persistence: No evidence of cron jobs, systemd units, launch agents, shell profile edits, or self-reinstall loops.
  • Lateral movement: No evidence of Kubernetes, Docker socket, cloud metadata, GitHub Actions workflow injection, or token reuse behavior.
  • Obfuscation/loader: marshal.loads in cssutils/codec.py appears to restore codec incremental state, not to load an obfuscated payload or execute dynamic code.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • From the provided extracted text, there is no confirmed evidence of PyPI-only hidden payloads, unexpected native binaries, sudden dependency insertion, typosquatting, or wheel/sdist mismatch.
  • The pre-scan detected many URLs in documentation/tests/README files, including a raw.githubusercontent.com badge URL; based on the supplied evidence, these appear to be documentation/test/badge references rather than malicious exfiltration endpoints.

Additional Verification Needed

  • Only selected text from 324 extracted files was provided. The pre-scan mentioned unusual .top domain references in docs/html/_static/jquery.js; the original file should be reviewed. With the current input, there is insufficient evidence linking those references to install/import-time execution or credential theft.
  • For stronger distribution-integrity assessment, compare the PyPI sdist/wheel against the upstream source tag and check for wheel-vs-sdist differences.
